new_statements.quote: [p.86] Shangaci is a tonal language with each mora being either high or low. [...] In nominal and verbal tonology, high tones are assigned on lexical and morphological grounds respectively. [p.88, 3.1] Words that are uttered in isolation always have penultimate lengthening (PUL) applied to them. Within a sentence PUL marks the end of a phonological phrase. [p.89] As shown in Downing (2004: 122) and Hyman (2009) penult stress is a widespread phenomenon in Bantu languages and its most common phonetic correlate is vowel lengthening. [...] The fact that Shangaci has PUL, although neighbouring Makhuwa variants as well as Koti lack it, need therefore not come as a surprise.
new_statements.citation: Devos, Maud. 2013. Vowel length in Shangaci: when lexical vowel length and penultimate lengthening co-occur. Africana Linguistica 19: 85-107. doi:10.3406/aflin.2013.1018
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened the held text layer of Devos 2013, from the Persée PDF alongside it). All three quoted passages are present verbatim at the stated locators (the [...] marks genuine omissions): p.86 sec. 2 'Shangaci is a tonal language with each mora being either high or low. Tone assignment rules... In nominal and verbal tonology, high tones are assigned on lexical and morphological grounds respectively.'; p.88 sec. 3.1 'Words that are uttered in isolation always have penultimate lengthening (PUL) applied to them. Within a sentence PUL marks the end of a phonological phrase.'; p.89 'As shown in Downing (2004: 122) and Hyman (2009) penult stress is a widespread phenomenon in Bantu languages and its m…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Shangaci is a tone language (lexical H in nouns, morphologically assigned H in verbs, with H doubling and retraction); it has no lexical stress, but the penultimate syllable of every phonological phrase (hence of every word in isolation/citation form) is automatically lengthened, which the author identifies with Bantu penult stress; a phrase-final H retracts onto the lengthened penult.
new_statements.exceptions: PUL does not apply phrase-medially (e.g. noun + possessive phrase together, so the noun's penult is not lengthened); PUL neutralises lexical vowel length in phrase-final penults; Portuguese loans show long vowels where Portuguese had stress; neighbouring Makhuwa varieties and Koti lack PUL.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological phrase, not the word: penult lengthening marks the right edge of the phonological phrase; citation forms (words in isolation) always show it. Author notes (fn. 12) that no controlled acoustic study has been done.
new_statements.identity_note: Devos's 'Shangaci' (2008-2014 spelling) / 'Shangaji' (2016- spelling) is the language Glottolog files as Nathembo [nath1238], ISO 639-3 nte (Ethnologue name Nathembo; autonym Esakaji/Sakati); Glottolog itself attaches Devos's Shangaci publications to nath1238. Described variety: the coastal village north of Angoche, Nampula province; a Makhuwa (P30) x Swahili contact language closely related to Koti [koti1238]. No dialect differentiation is discussed.

sources.citation: Devos, Maud. 2013. Vowel length in Shangaci: when lexical vowel length and penultimate lengthening co-occur. Africana Linguistica 19: 85-107. doi:10.3406/aflin.2013.1018
sources.quote: [p.86] Shangaci is a tonal language with each mora being either high or low. [...] In nominal and verbal tonology, high tones are assigned on lexical and morphological grounds respectively. [p.88, 3.1] Words that are uttered in isolation always have penultimate lengthening (PUL) applied to them. Within a sentence PUL marks the end of a phonological phrase. [p.89] As shown in Downing (2004: 122) and Hyman (2009) penult stress is a widespread phenomenon in Bantu languages and its most common phonetic correlate is vowel lengthening. [...] The fact that Shangaci has PUL, although neighbouring Makhuwa variants as well as Koti lack it, need therefore not come as a surprise.
sources.note: Sec. 2 (p.86): Shangaci is a tonal language, each mora H or L; H tones lexical in nouns, morphologically assigned in verbs, with H doubling and retraction. Sec. 3/3.1 (p.88): automatic penultimate lengthening (PUL) at the end of a phonological phrase; words in isolation always have PUL. p.89: PUL is treated as the Shangaci reflex of Bantu penult stress (Downing 2004, Hyman 2009), notable because neighbouring Makhuwa and Koti lack it. p.93: stressed syllables of Portuguese loans surface as long vowels. p.94: PUL neutralises lexical length in phrase-final penults.

sources.note: Nothing on stress; only incidental remarks on tonal patterns (predicative lowering of lexical H in nouns). Intro identifies Shangaci as a Makhuwa (P30) variant influenced by Swahili, c. 4000 speakers north of Angoche.
